cards.title: Why is a child saying 'Na-na, na-na-na!' so annoying?
cards.body: Explore why repetitive sounds from children can feel so frustrating to parents. Readers share insights on managing these annoying but developmentally normal behaviors.

cards.title: Partner's obnoxious conduct at sons' football matches
cards.body: A parent seeks advice on managing their partner's inappropriate behavior at their sons' sports events. Expert guidance on addressing anger and communication in long-term relationships.

cards.title: Halloween is looming – ditching cynicism for family magic
cards.body: A parent embraces Halloween celebrations as a meaningful moment of connection with their kids. From Day of the Dead traditions to Samhain, autumn festivities offer magic and bonding opportunities.

cards.title: Working parent logistics nightmare and school holiday breaks
cards.body: Parents juggle constant life admin while their children are in school, making quality time elusive. The article explores how school holiday scheduling affects working parents' ability to spend meaningful time with kids.

cards.title: Behavioral approaches work for neurodivergent kids
cards.body: Parents are often told behavioral strategies don't work for neurodivergent children, but rigorous research proves otherwise. Behavioral approaches show effectiveness even with autistic kids who avoid everyday demands.

cards.title: Beyond 'Make This Go Away': Kids and mental health
cards.body: Teaching kids to express and understand their emotions builds crucial life skills. When children know they can share their emotional experiences, they learn to process their inner lives effectively.

cards.title: How to manage after-school restraint collapse
cards.body: Some children vent frustration at home immediately after school ends, a phenomenon called restraint collapse. Five practical steps can help parents manage this common behavior more effectively.

cards.title: Why boomer parents and millennial daughters miscommunicate
cards.body: Loving parents and adult daughters often misunderstand each other due to hidden emotional labor. Three everyday phrases reveal how generational differences create unintentional conflict.

cards.title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained?
cards.body: A third of school starters in the West Midlands weren't toilet-trained before starting school. The article examines why potty-training delays are increasingly common among young children.
